participants.basis: Exactly two people speak. Although presented as a friendly conversation rather than a formal timed debate, Sechler advances a Christian plausibility case and Clifton advances the opposing hiddenness-and-hell challenge; they directly test each other's reasons throughout the assessed window.

format.motionInterpretation: Sechler defends a qualified Christian account through probabilistic commitment, salvation without a theology test, virtue formation, freedom, and potentially nontraditional accounts of hell. Clifton argues that nonresistant nonbelief, doxastic involuntarism, salvation costs, and parental-love analogies make a loving relational God implausible. Preserve both speakers' qualifications and concessions.
